messages:
jess: Hey team — getting an urgent customer escalation (ACME) about multi-tool calls coming back mis-associated. They call two tools in parallel and sometimes the tool_result payloads are attached to the wrong tool id.

raj: Ugh. Do we have a correlation id / example request?

jess: Yep. Correlation-ID: 0f3a9c4b-acc1-4d2a-b7f3-f2a9d8e6c001, request-id: r-1843219876. Observed in prod (us-west-2) and also hit in a Dedicated test cluster. SDK v2.4.1.

jess: Minimal request body (simplified):
```json
{
  "input": "summarize and then translate:",
  "tool_calls": [
    {"tool": "fetch_docs", "call_id": "call-A", "args": {"query":"invoice 123"}},
    {"tool": "translate_es", "call_id": "call-B", "args": {"lang":"es"}}
  ],
  "mode": "parallel"
}
```

jess: Expected: responses.map by call_id. Actual: sometimes translate_es result ends up under call-A and fetch_docs result under call-B.

sam: Do you have the raw response we returned to the customer? (mask PII)

jess: Pasted sanitized response below — note call ids:
```json
{
  "request_id":"r-1843219876",
  "tool_results": [
    {"call_id":"call-A","tool":"fetch_docs","result":{"snippet":"..."}},
    {"call_id":"call-B","tool":"translate_es","result":{"translated":"factura 123"}}
  ]
}
```

jess: But our internal tool logs show translate completed first and returned tokenized output that matches the snippet labeled call-A in the response. Log excerpt: 
```
[1843219876.112] tool=translate_es call_id=call-B finished (latency=120ms) result_id=tr-9c1
[1843219876.115] tool=fetch_docs call_id=call-A finished (latency=320ms) result_id=fd-42a
[1843219876.116] response_assembler attached result_id=tr-9c1 to call_id=call-A
```

raj: Hm looks like the assembler matched by completion order rather than call_id. Any chance call_id was duplicated client-side?

jess: Verified call_ids are unique in the incoming payload. We also saw mismatches across ~0.7% of calls over a 2h window. Not correlated to a single model or hardware type.

sam: Is this happening only when we route to multiple backends concurrently? Or also when same backend handles both?

jess: Both. Observed when fetch_docs hits search cluster A and translate hits runtime pool B, and also when both land on the same pool under high load.

support-bot: Created ticket RED-INC-5423 for customer ACME (priority: high).

infra-bot: New incident created: INC-5423. Pager duty notified.

emily: Short-term mitigation: serialize the tool calls (mode=\"sequential\") or include an opaque external_call_tag in args that we echo back from the tool execution layer so customer can reconcile. We should also add a strict binding check in response_assembler: require matching call_id before attaching.

raj: Good idea. Jess — please include stack traces + the full log bundle and the captured request/response for RED-INC-5423. Also note SDK version + deploy hashes.

jess: Will dump logs and repro steps. Quick repro I gave to SRE (curl):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/invoke \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"input":"x","tool_calls":[{"tool":"fetch_docs","call_id":"call-A"},{"tool":"translate_es","call_id":"call-B"}],"mode":"parallel"}'
```

jess: With a simple loop of 200 concurrent requests I reproduced ~1% mis-associations within 5 minutes. I saved the request/response pairs and logs in the incident folder.

sam: Thanks — tagging @sre and @runtime. Please avoid telling customer to run concurrent parallel calls until we fix.

jess: Noted. Customer notified that we're investigating and provided temporary workaround (sequential mode).

emily: I'm putting a small hotfix in the assembler to validate call_id equality before mapping. Will PR and run canary.

raj: Once PR is in, let's run the same 200-concurrent repro for 30 minutes and validate no mis-assoc. Also add unit test that simulates out-of-order completions.

jess: Thanks everyone. I'll attach logs to RED-INC-5423 and follow up when SRE has results. :thumbsup:
